jd:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

 Position Summary 
 The Statistical Programming Summer Internship provides a master’s-level student with the opportunity to apply programming, data science, automation, and emerging technologies to real-world challenges in clinical development.
The intern will work alongside experienced statistical programmers and cross-functional partners on a defined project focused on improving the efficiency, quality, or scalability of clinical data and statistical programming processes. Depending on project assignment, the work may involve clinical trial data and metadata, CDISC standards, SAS or R programming, Python-based automation, generative AI, validation and testing, or development of reusable programming solutions. The internship is intended to provide hands-on experience in a regulated pharmaceutical environment while giving the intern an opportunity to develop a practical solution, evaluate its effectiveness, document findings, and present recommendations to the broader team.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 -Work with a project supervisor and subject-matter experts to understand a statistical programming, clinical data, automation, or technology-related business problem and translate it into clear project objectives and deliverables.
-Design, develop, test, and document a prototype, analytical workflow, automation solution, or reusable programming approach.
-Apply programming languages such as SAS, R, and/or Python to data processing, analysis, automation, validation, or clinical programming use cases.
-Explore opportunities to use automation, generative AI, metadata-driven approaches, or open-source technologies to improve programming efficiency and quality. 
 -Work with structured data and metadata and, where applicable, gain exposure to CDISC standards such as SDTM, ADaM, and Define-XML.
-Perform structured testing and validation to evaluate the accuracy, consistency, reliability, and limitations of developed solutions.
-Compare results against existing processes or established approaches and clearly document differences, assumptions, limitations, and areas requiring human review.
-Collaborate with statistical programmers and other cross-functional stakeholders to gather requirements, obtain feedback, and refine solutions.
-Prepare clear technical documentation and summarize project findings, lessons learned, and recommendations.
-Present the completed project and demonstrate key outcomes to Statistical Programming colleagues and other stakeholders at the conclusion of the internship. 
   
 Qualifications & Experience 
 Required Qualifications 
-Currently enrolled in a Master’s degree program in Statistics, Biostatistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics, or a closely related quantitative discipline.
-Must be continuing in the Master’s degree program following completion of the internship.
-Experience programming in at least one of the following: SAS, R, or Python.
-Foundational knowledge of data manipulation, analytical programming, statistical computing, software development, or related quantitative methods.
-Demonstrated ability to learn new programming languages, tools, and technical concepts.
-Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
-Strong written and verbal communication skills.

 Preferred Qualifications and Experience 
-Experience with two or more of SAS, R, and Python.
-Familiarity with Git/GitHub, Visual Studio Code, automated testing, or reproducible programming workflows.
-Knowledge of clinical trial data or experience working with healthcare, life sciences, or other regulated data.
-Familiarity with CDISC standards, particularly SDTM, ADaM, Define-XML, or clinical trial metadata.
-Experience or coursework involving generative AI, large language models, automation, software testing, APIs, XML/JSON, or data visualization.
-Interest in applying emerging technology to improve clinical development and statistical programming processes.
   
 Core Competencies 
 -Analytical Thinking: Able to break down complex problems, evaluate evidence, and develop practical solutions.
-Programming and Technical Learning: Demonstrates a strong foundation in programming and the ability to quickly learn new languages, tools, standards, and technologies.
-Innovation and Curiosity: Curious about emerging technologies and willing to explore new approaches to improve existing processes.
-Quality and Attention to Detail: Produces accurate, well-documented work and recognizes the importance of testing, validation, traceability, and reproducibility.
-Problem Solving: Able to identify issues, investigate root causes, compare alternative approaches, and recommend appropriate solutions.
-Collaboration: Works effectively with mentors, statistical programmers, and cross-functional partners and incorporates feedback constructively.
-Communication: Able to explain technical concepts, methods, findings, and limitations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
-Accountability and Initiative: Self-motivated and able to manage assigned work, communicate progress, and deliver agreed project objectives within the internship timeline.
-Responsible Use of Technology: Understands the importance of data privacy, appropriate human oversight, and responsible use of automation and AI in a regulated environment.

 We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

We invest funds for the pension plans of the federal public service, the Canadian Forces, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and the Reserve Force. Headquartered in Ottawa, PSP Investments has its principal business office in Montréal and offices in New York, London and Hong Kong. 

 Capturing and leading complex global investments requires us to work as one to seize valuable opportunities, in close collaboration with some of the world’s top companies. At PSP Investments, you’ll join a team of motivated and engaged professionals, dedicated to propelling our organization further than ever before.

• Comfort with MS Office / Microsoft 365; exposure to the Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate) is an asset 
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and ask good questions 
• Good written and verbal communication skills

If you require any accommodation for any part of the recruitment process, please let us know.

Get started on an exciting career at Element! 

 Element employees make a difference in the lives of others every day. We are re-defining the fleet management industry to be people first, then business – delivering on our promise of a superior client experience. This takes hard work and innovation, and we need more like-minded people on our team. 
 
 Build and deploy practical AI solutions from business problem to working pilot. 

 THE OPPORTUNITY 

 The AI Platform Engineering team brings artificial intelligence solutions directly to the business teams it serves. As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Intern, you will join discovery conversations, learn how operational workflows work, and help design, build, and deploy 

 AI agents, tools, and intelligent workflows on Element's enterprise agentic AI platform. Working alongside senior engineers, you will contribute scoped solutions from prototype through pilot, translate business needs into technical designs, and bring field feedback back to the platform team. You will receive structured mentorship, clearly scoped ownership, and regular feedback while gaining hands-on exposure to production AI delivery.

 WHAT YOU WILL OWN 

• Build and deploy AI agents, tools, and intelligent workflows on Element's agentic AI platform for scoped business use cases, with guidance from senior engineers. 
• Integrate agents with enterprise data sources, internal APIs, and business systems using Python and/or TypeScript within platform governance, security, and permission boundaries. 
• Apply retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool and function calling, and multi-step orchestration patterns using established platform patterns and templates. 
• Join discovery sessions with internal business teams, document workflows and pain points, and help translate needs into use-case specifications, agent designs, and acceptance criteria. 
• Support demos and pilot rollouts, gather user feedback, track adoption and outcome metrics, and create lightweight enablement materials such as quick-start guides, demos, and FAQs. 
• Write evaluation cases and test datasets, use observability and tracing tools to investigate failures, and contribute to guardrails, fallbacks, error handling, documentation, and runbooks. 
 YOU SHOULD CONSIDER THIS ROLE IF: 

 You are curious, comfortable with ambiguity, and eager to move between coding and collaboration with business users.
 
• You are currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field, with at least one term of study remaining or graduating within the internship window. 
• You have hands-on experience through academic projects, co-ops, internships, hackathons, or personal projects building software that integrates large language models, machine learning models, or AI services. 
• You have working proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript and are comfortable with REST or GraphQL APIs, JSON, and Git-based workflows. 
• You have foundational familiarity with LLM application patterns such as prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool or function calling, and agentic orchestration frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK, or similar. 
• You have some exposure to cloud environments, preferably AWS services such as Bedrock, Lambda, and DynamoDB, and to containerization with Docker. 
• You can ask clear questions of non-technical stakeholders, demo working software, and write clear documentation. Preferred experience includes familiarity with LLM evaluation frameworks, AI observability tooling, vector databases, or front-end development with React/Next.js.

 YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO TELL US 

• About an AI or software project you built, including the problem you were solving, the technical approach you chose, and what you learned from the result. 
• How you have used Python and/or TypeScript, APIs, or cloud services to connect systems, data, models, or user-facing functionality. 
• How you have tested, evaluated, debugged, or improved an AI-enabled application or workflow based on observed behaviour or user feedback. 
• How you have explained or demonstrated technical work to a non-technical audience and incorporated their feedback. 
 WHY ELEMENT 

 At Element Fleet Management, this internship gives you the opportunity to work on practical AI solutions that connect technology with real business workflows. You will learn alongside senior engineers, contribute to pilots used by internal business teams, and help improve the enterprise AI platform through field feedback and reusable patterns. Element's purpose is to Move the world through intelligent mobility. In this role, you can contribute by helping build safe, useful AI-enabled processes that reduce friction and manual effort.

 LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT 

• Location: 1 Adelaide St. E., Toronto, ON 
• Working arrangement: Hybrid 
 COMPENSATION 

 The hiring base salary for this position is $54,400 - $74,800 annually. This range represents the Company's good-faith estimate of the expected base salary at the time of posting. Salary ranges may vary based on the geographic location where the work is performed. The salary range listed in this posting applies only to the location identified. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including the successful candidate's qualifications, knowledge, skills, experience, internal pay equity, and relevant market data. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may participate in annual incentive programs, including bonuses, commissions, or other incentive compensation, as applicable to the role. Element also offers a comprehensive benefits package, which may include health insurance, tuition reimbursement, and retirement savings plans.

 Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the country where the position is based. Element Fleet Management does not provide sponsorship or support for obtaining or maintaining work authorization for this position. 
 
 What’s in it for You

•  Comprehensive health and welfare benefits that serve the needs of you and your family and foster a culture of wellness (for qualified roles)
•  Additional benefits and amenities, including paid time-off programs (vacation, sick leave, and holidays) (for qualified roles)

Job Details: 

 Job Description: 
 Join Us in Shaping the Future
 
At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
 
The Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
 
Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.
 
Responsibilities
• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

 Success in This Role 
 • Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies. 
 • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills. 
 • Clear written and verbal communication. 
 • Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed. 
 • Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.

 Qualifications: 
 Minimum Qualifications 
 • Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline. 
 • Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area. 
 • Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems. 
 • Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions. 

 Preferred Qualifications
